notes: CITATION CORRECTION CHECKED: the correct canonical paper for the 100STYLE dataset is Mason, Starke & Komura's 'Real-Time Style Modelling of Human Locomotion via Feature-Wise Transformations and Local Motion Phases' (PACM CGIT / SIGGRAPH 2022, DOI 10.1145/3522618, arXiv preprint 2201.04439) -- NOT 'Local Motion Phases for Learning Multi-Contact Character Movements' (that is a different, earlier Starke et al. SIGGRAPH 2020 paper on character control, unrelated to this dataset). Verified via web search and the arXiv/ACM listings; no correction to the paper identity was ultimately needed against the task brief, only confirmation. Dataset facts (verified via zenodo.org/records/8127870 and the author's project page ianxmason.github.io/100style, which redirects to ianxmason.com/100style/): 4,055,978 frames at 60 fps = ~67,600 s = ~1,127 minutes (~18.8 hours) of BVH skeletal motion-capture data, captured with an Xsens inertial mocap suit, covering 100 distinct locomotion styles performed by a single actor. Licence CC BY 4.0 (attribution required; the project page suggests crediting 'The 100STYLE Dataset - Ian Mason' for creative/commercial reuse). Fully open, no request form or gating -- this is the designated smoke-test source for HALO's synthetic-IMU pipeline given its permissive licence and single-file Zenodo distribution. paper.pdf here is the arXiv preprint (2201.04439), which is the same paper content as the published PACM CGIT version; ACM's own PDF sits behind the ACM Digital Library paywall. Verified 2026-09-09.
